newsitem.title: VANUATU: Vanuatu troops arrested over presidental abduction.
newsitem.headline: Vanuatu troops arrested over presidental abduction.

text.p: More than 100 members of Vanuatu's paramilitary force, which adbucted the South Pacific nation's president last month over a pay dispute, were arrested on Tuesday, said Justice Minister Father Walter Lini.
In a national radio broadcast, Lini said members of the Vanuatu Mobile Force (VMF) were arrested in the early hours of Tuesday.
Police told Reuters that 138 of the 300-strong VMF, which is effectively Vanuatu's army, had been arrested.

"All those members involved in the October 12 operation have been arrested this morning and the law and order of Vanuatu is now in the hands of the Vanuatu Police Force," said Lini from the capital Port Vila.
Lini said the VMF were taken by surprise, but offered no resistance, and were taken to Vila Central Prison.
At a news conference in Port Vila later, Lini said all those arrested will be prosecuted in relation to the abduction, but he could not say what charges would be laid.

"All the members of the force will be prosecuted and those whom the court finds not guilty will be allowed to return to the force, but the government will make sure they take an oath of allegiance before they return," Lini said.
Residents in Port Vila said the tropical South Pacific port was calm, but that the arrests had surprised them.
The VMF claim the government has failed to pay them special duty allowances amounting to US$1.1 million since 1992.
On October 12, the VMF abducted Vanuatu President Jean-Marie Leye from his home and forced him to fly to a nearby island for several hours.

The VMF asked the president to then represent them at an emergency cabinet meeting later that day over the allowance dispute. The cabinet resolved to pay the VMF the back allowance by the end of October, but no payment has yet been made.
The entire 300-strong VMF also went on strike in October over the pay dispute.
